question.text: A trader buys a USDINR 83 call at Rs. 0.10. At expiry USDINR is 82.75. What is the loss?

answer.text: No loss — the option is automatically rolled over

explanation.text: The Logic: At expiry USDINR = 82.75, the 83 call is out-of-the-money because spot is below the strike. The buyer does not exercise the option, and the maximum loss equals the premium paid: Rs. 0.10 per unit (Rs. 100 per lot at 1,000 units per lot). The Trap: Option B (Rs. 0.25) does not match the premium paid (Rs. 0.10). Option C (Rs. 82.75) is the spot rate, not a loss figure. Option D is wrong because exchange-traded options are not automatically rolled over. Note: Trap-sentence truncation repaired; explanation rewritten with a clean OTM call rationale and accurate option-letter references.
